newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistan expects ministers meeting with India.
newsitem.headline: Pakistan expects ministers meeting with India.

text.p: Indian and Pakistani foreign ministers are expected to meet in New Delhi next week after a Non-Aligned Movement ministerial conference there on April 7-8, the Pakistani Foreign Ministry said on Saturday.
Pakistani Foreign Minister Gohar Ayub Khan, who left for New Delhi on Saturday, is expected to hold bilateral meetings with his NAM counterparts, a ministry statement said.
"The Foreign Minister is also expected to hold a meeting with his Indian counterpart Inder Kumar Gujral before his return to Pakistan on 9 April," it said.

On Wednesday, a Foreign Ministry spokesman said Ayub Khan had received an invitation from Gujral for a meeting at the end of the NAM conference and that "our minister...would certainly meet the Indian Foreign Minister".

But he said he was "not quite certain" what affect the Indian domestic crisis, created by the withdrawal of vital support by Congress party to Prime Minister H.K. Deve Gowda's government, would have on the meeting.
Last month India and Pakistan resumed high-level talks that had broken off in early 1994 owing to deep differences over the divided Himalayan region of Kashmir.
The two nations' foreign secretaries -- the highest-ranking civil servants in their foreign ministries -- ended four days of upbeat talks on March 31 and agreed to meet again in Islamabad.
But they failed to set dates, partly because of the political turmoil in New Delhi where Deve Gowda faces a vote of confidence in parliament on April 11.
Earlier this week, senior officials said they believed the political crisis in India would prevent Gujral and Ayub Khan from holding substantive discussions.
But Gujral told Reuters on Friday that the talks would go ahead as planned, and he would be seeing Khan on the sidelines of the NAM meeting and after that.
